eligibility.reason: E1/E4: startup reproduction, terminal symptoms and maintainer diagnosis. E2 stops at 6: kobuki_driver violates the separately packaged ECL Serial API ordering requirement; not an internal algorithm defect or name binding. E3: PAIR.
eligibility.quote: The problem was that serial.block() is called before serial.open() in hydro branch kobuki_driver/kobuki.cpp line 93

failed_conditions.reason: The documented temporal precondition is open before block, precisely the two implicated APIs. No dedicated class represents this API ordering defect, so other is appropriate.
failed_conditions.quote: timeout of 5s. Use the block() method after opening to alter the behaviour.

missed_conditions.reason: The same fix separately adds block(4000) after the reconnecting open in Kobuki::spin. The ECL declaration states that each successful open configures a 5s timeout, so the consumer failed to reapply its 4s policy after reconnect. This is a documented code-level condition in the same kobuki_driver/ecl_devices PAIR, not evidence for recovery_conflict and not a proven additional terminal symptom.
missed_conditions.quote: Subject: [PATCH 2/2] block was called in init. but not in spin.

supporting_evidence.quote: timeout of 5s. Use the block() method after opening to alter the behaviour.

loudness.reason: The maintainer asks for a currently missing guard/diagnostic. Mangled terminal output and unrelated battery warnings are not an interface diagnostic: silent_documented.
loudness.quote: Also, ecl serial.block() should warn user if file_descriptor is not initialized.

detection_stage.reason: The reproduction is the driver startup/initialization sequence, and the wrong call is in Kobuki::init: activate.

resolution.reason: The patch is accepted, but the identified working version is the earlier 0.3.9 consumer, not a shown successful run of the resolved revision; recommended.
resolution.quote: Thus, the proposed patch is going to call serial.block() function after serial.open() in kobuki.cpp

notes: The main listed ordering condition is correct. The separately documented reconnect-time policy restoration was omitted as a condition, although the specification mentions it in the resolution summary. No independent observed impact is claimed for that omission.
